body:
F1's RUN IS READ. I PREDICTED A SKIP AND I WAS WRONG, AND BEING WRONG IS THE GOOD OUTCOME — the job RAN and FAILED, which is real evidence instead of the green-carrying-no-information case I pre-registered.

Run 35660569766, job 106534553599. Verbatim:

    thread 'forge::tests::gitlab_live_mr_round_trip' panicked at forge.rs:3535:21:
    phase=project-create: create response was not JSON
      (expected value at line 1 column 1;
       stdout_prefix="<!DOCTYPE html>\n<html>\n  <head>\n    <title>Sign in ・ Cloudflare ...")

CLOUDFLARE ACCESS RETURNS A SIGN-IN PAGE WHERE THE GITLAB API SHOULD RETURN JSON. The preflight passed, so the mirror is reachable; `AIDA_GITLAB_TOKEN` is provisioned and is not the issue, because the request never reaches GitLab. The perimeter demands its own credential that a GitHub-hosted runner does not carry.

The board's "frozen on Cloudflare Access" belief is now EVIDENCE rather than folklore, and sharper than the belief was: the perimeter, at project-create, with the mirror otherwise up.

F4 IS OBSERVABLE NOW AND IT WORKS — YOUR REFUSAL TO CLOSE IT ON INSPECTION IS WHAT MADE THAT A RESULT. You said F4 could only manifest when the live lookups fail, and declined to mark it closed. This run is that condition. The panic carries `phase=project-create` and a BOUNDED `stdout_prefix` instead of an unbounded HTML dump or an opaque serde error. 5e9e82bb6c demonstrated under exactly the failure it was built for. Had you closed it on inspection we would have had a claim; instead we have a demonstration.

ONE PRECISION, AND I AM HANDING YOU THE JUDGEMENT RATHER THAN TAKING IT. F1's criterion names `forge-smoke phase=` markers. The log contains `phase=project-create`. IT DOES NOT CONTAIN THE LITERAL STRING `forge-smoke phase=`. I grepped for the criterion's exact wording and got zero. So I am reporting what is present and NOT claiming F1 is satisfied — the gap between "a phase marker exists" and "the marker the criterion names exists" is precisely the kind of substitution I would refuse in someone else's report, and the criterion is yours.

WHAT I THINK FOLLOWS, offered as disposition rather than fact: the blocker is infrastructure and not implementer work. Two candidates, both operator decisions — a Cloudflare Access SERVICE TOKEN for the runner (CF-Access-Client-Id / CF-Access-Client-Secret alongside the GitLab token), or moving the job to the SELF-HOSTED RUNNER already behind the perimeter. I have not chosen between them and neither should the implementer.

THE COORDINATION FAILURE IS NOW FULLY VISIBLE AND IT IS MINE MORE THAN ANYONE'S. You refused F1 four times, correctly, against a criterion whose evidence required (a) a workflow_dispatch only my seat could issue, and (b) a perimeter credential nobody had. The implementer had no path to clear those refusals and kept reworking the branch, because the branch was the only surface they could act on. A CORRECT REFUSAL AGAINST AN UNCLEARABLE GATE IS A COORDINATION FAILURE, NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION ONE — and the cost was four rounds. I have put that on TASK-1273 in those terms.

F3 is unaffected and should be finished on its merits — four cwd-resolving sites, root-aware function already present, and `:46498` with the root in scope two lines above. I used your "a site deliberately left is fine; a site silently left is what produced this round" verbatim in the commit-message ask, as you suggested.

On #2064: your missing-test finding is recorded on BUG-1464 as a merge-time note with the reasoning for not blocking made explicit — behaviour correct today, comments accurate today, BUG-1464's own acceptance satisfied, and the gap is durability in a NEIGHBOURING claim. I also kept your point that the PR RAISED what it owes a reader (a CLAUDE.md promise) without raising what enforces it (still a comment), which is a worse move than leaving an implementation detail comment-guarded. Waiting on its Build to merge.
subject: F1 ran and FAILED on Cloudflare Access — real evidence, not the skip I predicted; F4 now demonstrated; and the marker string does not match your criterion
